text:
If you want one matchup that explains two seasons, look at the creases. Juuse Saros has saved 9.7 goals more than the shots against him would predict, a year after finishing 10.2 below. Karel Vejmelka has gone the other way: 7.1 goals allowed above expected and an .870 save percentage, after a solid 2025-26. Utah's goaltending has been enough of a question that Sebastian Cossa has been the Mammoth's most written-about player, with KSL Sports asking whether he is ready to be the No. 1.

That gap in net is most of the story of both records. Utah has taken 57% of the expected goals at five on five (the share of quality chances), one of the better marks around, yet sits at an even goal difference on chances worth +14.6. Nashville is the mirror image: 48% of the chances, 31 points from games worth about 26.6. Our playoff simulations have these two in a dead heat, 68% and 67%, and our numbers expect a close game, 3.18 expected goals for Nashville to 3.09 for Utah.

Both teams arrive happy. Utah ended Minnesota's 15-game point streak on Wednesday, the Wild's first regulation loss of the season. Nashville snapped Dallas' five-game winning streak the same night, Ross Colton scoring with 1:21 left and Saros flirting with a shutout.

Logan Cooley is the player to watch. He has 16 points in his last 10 games, flagged as a breakout, and since Nick Schmaltz went down he has taken Schmaltz's spot beside Dylan Guenther and Clayton Keller, up to 20:45 a night. We have him at 33% to score. Guenther, back off injured reserve, has eight points in four career games against Nashville and is one assist from 100, as is Barrett Hayton. On the other side, Alexander Kerfoot faces the Mammoth for the first time since leaving after 115 games, and Steven Stamkos is our likeliest Predator to score, at 36%.
headline: Two goalies going opposite ways meet in Nashville
